💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that one of the names you can find on a memorial wall in GTA 6 belongs to the daughter of a Rockstar Games developer.
  • Stone shared a video of his visit to the memorial on X on November 27.
  • In a recent development, as Dexerto reports, Stone and his wife had experienced several miscarriages before a scan in 2023 revealed that their unborn daughter had a severe case of spina bifida.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that one of the names you can find on a memorial wall in GTA 6 belongs to the daughter of a Rockstar Games developer. Bradley Stone, a lead game tools programmer at Rockstar, has shared the story behind the inscription and thanked the studio for including it in the game. He and his wife lost their daughter Evelyn in 2023, while GTA 6 was still in development.

Stone shared a video of his visit to the memorial on X on November 27. The video shows Evelyn Stone's name with the date April 8, 2023.

In a recent development, as Dexerto reports, Stone and his wife had experienced several miscarriages before a scan in 2023 revealed that their unborn daughter had a severe case of spina bifida. After further examinations, the couple learned that she wouldn't survive and had to undergo a medical termination five months into the pregnancy.

Stone recalled how difficult it was to leave the hospital without their daughter. He also spoke of his wife's courage throughout the ordeal, which involved nearly a full day of labor. The couple has since welcomed another daughter after going through more difficulties in the years that followed.

According to recent reports, stone thanked Rockstar for giving his family somewhere to remember Evelyn and for supporting him through his grief. He also mentioned the memorial helped “to show this game was made by real people.” He ended his post with a message to his daughter.

“You will forever be in our hearts,” he wrote.

Rockstar hadn't even released the first GTA 6 trailer when Stone and his wife lost Evelyn. That came eight months later, in December 2023. For those of us following the game, the years since then have been spent poring over trailers and wondering when we'd finally get to play it. Reading Stone's account puts that long wait into perspective.

If you'd like to visit the memorial yourself, you'll find it at Deep Roots Memorial Sanctuary, just north of Hamlet. You can also download Rockstar's official Leonida map to help get your bearings if you're unfamiliar with that part of the state. Stone isn't the first Rockstar employee to have shared the significance of one of the inscriptions there since the game came out.

According to recent reports, as GAMES.GG reported earlier this week, Rockstar QA developer Matt Green's mother, Beverly, is also commemorated at the sanctuary. He recalled begging her for a copy of GTA Vice City as a kid. She was reluctant at first but eventually agreed, and Green credits that purchase with sparking the interest that led him to a career at Rockstar.

According to recent reports, she was proud of his work on GTA 6, but passed away in March this year, before he could show her the finished game. Production designer Terrance Radcliff also lost two family members during development, his father Elhuntry and his first daughter Jade. Their names appear beside one another on the wall. Radcliff shared the tribute on November 22, as the launch week came to a close, explaining how much it meant to him to have both of them commemorated in the game.

What's particularly nice about the sanctuary is that it exists as an actual place within the world rather than a dedication that most of us would miss in the end credits. It's a place that the developers and their families can return to long after they've finished working on the game.

It's a place that the developers and their families can return to long after they've finished working on the game.

From subtle nods to previous games to an Easter egg that lets you revisit the original Vice City, there's plenty for longtime GTA fans to discover in Leonida. The names at Deep Roots carry a much more personal significance, though. I'm glad Stone, Green and Radcliff chose to share their stories with us, and that Rockstar gave them a place to honor their loved ones.

Recent findings suggest that ubisoft have laid off 166 developers, with this latest round of cuts at the Assassin's Creed and Far Cry publishers taking place at two of their studios in Eastern Canada. Both studios affected, Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, had a hand in last year's Assassin's Creed Shadows, with Montreal especially being a major and long-tenured development hub for the tech giant.

Both IGN and GamesIndustry.biz report that the cuts, which amount to just under 4% studios' total combined headcount, affected staff working on recently cancelled or significantly changed projects.

Sources indicate that "Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations," Ubisoft remarked in a statement handed to both sites. "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

Industry observers note that ubisoft Montreal are currently working on Assassin’s Creed Hexe, reportedly a witchy tale set during the time of the Holy Roman Empire, which switched creative directors earlier this ear and is one of the games Ubi are keen to get out of the door. What Quebec have been up to since Shadows shipped is less clear. They're a much smaller than Montreal and were founded in 2005.

Ubisoft have been carrying out mass cuts across their studios worldwide all the way through this year. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx. Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona. Long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm. Ubisoft's Paris HQ. Three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz. All have been subjected to some form of cuts or closure.

Meanwhile. changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Solidarity to all of the Ubisoft workers who've been affected by these layoffs in Montreal and Quebec.

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

Sources indicate that the Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

The first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

The ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

The more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

Badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

Heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

We also recently updated our guides on how to catch Frostspore fish - and if you’re into cooking, how to obtain every recipe and variant. If you haven’t already, definitely see if you missed any of these Heartopia codes, too.

#167922. Talking Point: Ocarina Of Time Revolutionised The 3D Swordfight, But How Does The Remake Hold Up In A Vintage Year For Clashing Blades?

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1092 w)
📖 Baca

Talking Point: Ocarina Of Time Revolutionised The 3D Swordfight, But How Does The Remake Hold Up In A Vintage Year For Clashing Blades?

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1092 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Forget the hubbub around Grand Theft Auto.
  • In a recent development, onimusha: Way of the Sword broke free of parryslop with exciting, flexible and immensely satisfying katana combat.
  • According to recent reports, it makes it a funny time for The Hero of Time to step back into the fray.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Forget the hubbub around Grand Theft Auto. Big Walk? Big deal. It’s all noise designed to distract us from 2026’s real legacy: that it’s been one of the best years on record for video game swordfighting.

In a recent development, onimusha: Way of the Sword broke free of parryslop with exciting, flexible and immensely satisfying katana combat. Blood of Dawnwalker’s directional combat recreated a scintillating sense of strike-and-counterstrike rhythm rather than asking players to hide behind defensive blocks. Then Phantom Blade Zero swans in with cinematic style and a dazzling flurry of wuxia sword strikes and somersaults.

According to recent reports, it makes it a funny time for The Hero of Time to step back into the fray. After all, the original N64 Ocarina of Time practically set the template for today’s sword-toting successors. Dark Souls, Onimusha, even Kingdom Hearts’ keyblade battles all follow in Link’s Kokiri bootprints.

Ocarina of Time famously defined the lock-on, circle strafing, and the basic choreography of action-game design. According to a 2011 Iwata Asks, that genre-defining 3D swordfighting had a charming origin story (after a fleeting moment where they considered making Ocarina of Time in first-person!). It came about thanks to a ninja show witnessed by co-director Toru Osawa and colleagues on a frankly enviable work excursion to the Toei Kyoto Studio Park.

Sources indicate that as Osawa remembered the Japanese period film reenactment, “a number of ninja were surrounding the main samurai, and one lashed out with a kusarigama [a sickle and chain weapon]. The lead samurai caught it with his left arm, the chain stretched tight, and the ninja moved in a circle around him.”.

Action choreography was the remaining matter for director Yoshiaki Koizumi. At that same ninja show, he spotted the action movie routine that helps Jackie Chan inexplicably survive every movie:.

Recent findings suggest that “First, one attacks while the others wait. When the first guy goes down, the next one steps in and so on [...] Watching that show at the studio park was a clue toward solving that problem. Z-targeting flags one particular opponent, telling the other enemies to wait.”.

In a recent development, that impeccable logic meant Link was safe from being mobbed by Keese swooping from offscreen in all directions. It was such a sound design principle that it continues to underpin action games today. But I suspect modern players no longer need to be handled with Koizumi’s kid gloves. Judging by the remake, Nintendo agrees.

Consider how Nintendo changed N64 Ocarina’s Forest Temple’s ominous fight against two Wolfos. Lock on to one, its counterpart scampers obediently into the background. Not so for the remake! These newly terrifying fiends aren’t just tankier, swifter, and more aggressive: they’ll conduct somersaulting tag-team switchups at will so you’re left to deal with a full health bar – just like the Lizalfos duo.

Sources indicate that it’s a lesson not every Ocarina successor learned. The latest Onimusha’s greatest flaw comes from how closely its mobs follow the age-old formula. Attacking one at a time, queuing up a procession of theatrical wind-up animations makes them trivially easy for a supremely talented Mushashi to attack, deflect, or even decapitate with a well-timed Issen counter. Dawnwalker’s usually not much better, sending vampire Brencis’s lackeys after you in patient succession.

In comparison, I have to commend Phantom Blade Zero for its willingness to toss out Koizumi’s Law, never passing up an opportunity to give players a well-deserved backstabbing.

But the remake’s multitude of combat changes go far beyond footwork and newly aggressive enemies. For all its modernising under-the-hood changes, playing it still feels like entering a mystical parallel universe where Sekiro never happened. I’m back with sword and shield in hand, without a high-risk, high-reward parry ability.

Even with its snappier, flashier but deeply familiar combat, it took some getting used to a gentler pace compared to more recent upstarts. I started my playthrough thoroughly parrybrained after spending nearly 100 hours playing Dawnwalker into Wolverine before finally catching up with Metroid Dread. When I returned to Hyrule, it was with fingers already twitching with anticipation at every incoming blow.

Shorn of a now-trendy stamina meter, the fact that locking on to an enemy automatically raises your shields reduces the jeopardy; when I get hit, it’s because I got greedy.

One problem: I was ready to parry but Link wasn’t. In fact, the remake felt close to playing Dark Souls using the almost obligatory sword-and-shield build (with a parry I never learned to use properly!). As our review rightly noted, it’s laudably true to the original game, not even touching The Wind Waker’s combat-geared flourishes like the jump-spin attacks that would follow five years later.

In a recent development, the result is combat that feels almost like a cautious game of chess. You bait a mistake or trigger a weakness before going for the stunlock. Shorn of a now-trendy stamina meter, the fact that locking on to an enemy automatically raises your shields reduces the jeopardy; when I get hit, it’s because I got greedy. It may no longer be dangerous to go alone, but at least we have a few tips to help up the ante – I just wouldn’t recommend a swordless run!

Along with the absent stamina and posture meters, Ocarina remake’s simpler combat blessedly ignores a more recent swordfighting innovation: light and heavy attacks. Generally, I can live without the added layer of combat timing fussiness the Soulslike dominion has given us. It also avoids the pitfalls introduced by Phantom Blade Zero, where single inputs translate into a continuous flurry of attacks that can feel unsatisfyingly disconnected from the buttons I’ve pressed.

It has been revealed that that’s not to say I wouldn’t say no to all modern embellishments. I’d love a high-powered combo finisher such as Wind Waker’s. But don’t forget: Ocarina already had a more entertaining means to deal a slow wind-up finishing blow capable of leaving its victim in a 6ft deep crater. It’s big, it’s bad, it’s the same height as your dad: it’s the Biggoron Sword!

But no matter the size of the sword he wields, Link’s return from the past has the vibe of a strangely youthful veteran checking in on his proteges. Musashi, Coen, and Soul are the fresh kids on the block, but they learned everything they know from their green-tunicked, rosy-cheeked master.

And if it ever comes down to a showdown, those newcomers simply aren’t getting past Link’s guard when he hasn’t got a stamina meter to wear down.

Keepsake County is finally OUT! And yes, it is deeply ironic that it wound up being today, of all days, that we got the green light to finally release, but here we are.".

Keepsake Country was supposed to release earlier this month, but seemingly got caught up in the backlog Valve are faced with that's undoubtedly been caused by genAI games. In any case, the burgle-em-up does look quite delightful. I'm not sure if I can quite put my finger on exactly why I get this feeling, but it calls to mind a more complex version of the kind of game you'd find on Cartoon Network's website back in the day (which is a high point of praise, I'd like to be clear).

Sources indicate that each house in Keepsake Country is procedurally generated, meaning you never quite know what to expect when you enter. There's lockpicking, resident tie upping, and of course stealing to be done, but it doesn't just stop at the house. Parking your car, for instance, is an key thing to consider; do you want it hidden so you're less likely to be discovered, or right at the front door so you can make a speedy escape? Not to mention you have to deal with the fuzz showing up at some point if you aren't quick enough!

Gear and the like can be improved between runs, meaning you can lockpick faster or delay the cops, it all seems quite systemically thoughtful. Very much some immersive sim vibes from this one, just on a much smaller scale. And most certainly worth considering picking up on a release day like today! If you're interested in doing so, you can pick it up on Steam right here.

Rockstar Explains Why GTA 6 Is Missing One of the Series' Most Iconic Weapons

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (654 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 has taken us back to Vice City for the first time in two decades, but one of the weapons I most associate with the city hasn't returned.
  • As Dexerto reports, Rockstar felt that the violence associated with the weapon would be too much for GTA 6.
  • It has been revealed that in an interview with VGC published on November 26, GTA 6 producer and Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson discussed some of the things that didn't make it into the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has taken us back to Vice City for the first time in two decades, but one of the weapons I most associate with the city hasn't returned. You can find chainsaws in Leonida, but you can't pick them up and use them like you could in GTA Vice City or San Andreas. Rockstar has now explained why.

As Dexerto reports, Rockstar felt that the violence associated with the weapon would be too much for GTA 6. It seems the studio is a little more selective about what it lets us get away with now that its games look this good.

It has been revealed that in an interview with VGC published on November 26, GTA 6 producer and Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson discussed some of the things that didn't make it into the game. Be warned that the interview contains story spoilers.

When asked about the absence of chainsaws, Nelson remarked, “I think it would have been too much for this game at this resolution and these characters.” He then added, “It’s not a resource thing.”.

Katanas, another staple of the PS2-era GTA games, are missing from the arsenal as well. It's a little odd to see a chainsaw lying around and not be able to pick it up, especially considering how interactive GTA 6 is compared to its predecessors.

I've always seen the chainsaw as more of a Hollywood and video game weapon than a practical one. In real life, using one against a person would hardly be as straightforward as the movies make it look. The saw could jam, and it would be an absolute mess. I can understand why Rockstar wouldn't want to depict that sort of gore in such detail, given how controversial the GTA series has been over the years.

Recent findings suggest that this is, after all, the same studio that gave us Manhunt. Manhunt 2 even ran into trouble with ratings boards before its release, and I don't think Rockstar is going back to the series anytime soon. It's one thing to make a horror game where the brutality is part of the premise, but quite another to let someone loose with a chainsaw in a modern recreation of Miami.

Recent findings suggest that for me, the chainsaw will always be associated with GTA Vice City. Colonel Cortez gives Tommy Vercetti one in Treacherous Swine, a fairly early mission in the game. It returned in San Andreas, both of the PSP GTA games, and Chinatown Wars. It was already absent from GTA 4 and GTA 5, though, so it's not as if every GTA game needs one.

Industry observers note that what I find more interesting about Nelson's answer is his reference to Jason and Lucia. There's a difference between what a protagonist would do in a cutscene and what you can get up to when you're not following the story. Part of the fun of the older GTA games was seeing how far you could stray from the character you were supposed to be playing.

Part of the fun of the older GTA games was seeing how far you could stray from the character you were supposed to be playing.

It has been revealed that CJ, for instance, had plenty of reasons to look after Grove Street, but San Andreas never stopped you from abandoning your responsibilities and spending an afternoon flying a jetpack around the desert. Even the weapons you could carry in that game included some pretty ridiculous choices that had little to do with CJ's life as a gang member.

Sources indicate that I can live without the chainsaw in GTA 6, especially if the alternative is something closer to Manhunt than the cartoonish violence of Vice City. I'd just hate to see the personalities of the protagonists become a reason to leave out some of the sillier weapons and activities in future GTA games.

Team Cherry promised us an update on Hollow Knight: Silksong's Sea of Sorrow DLC today, and thankfully it was not a tepid one where the studio gave the expansion a loose release window way off in the future. It was a far firmer reveal confirming that the free addition to Silksong will be here far sooner than you might have expected.

According to recent reports, the trailer for Sea of Sorrow was part of today's Cherry Time enhancement, giving us a first look at what horrors Hornet will be up against next. That first look at the expansion was coupled with the reveal that it will be available on December 11, 2026, so in just 13 days. The DLC will be free to all Silksong owners, no matter which platform you play on.

In a recent development, there is a lot crammed into what is a relatively short trailer showcasing what Sea of Sorrow has to offer. We're shown Hornet battling upcoming enemies, traversing new areas, and judging by the last thing we're shown right at the end of the trailer, she's learned how to fish. Hornet is shown standing on the shore, casting her thread into the water and immediately getting a bite.

Although Team Cherry promised Silksong would be getting an expansion, Hollow Knight fans were fearful because we've been there before. Silksong itself was originally supposed to be DLC for the original Hollow Knight. However, the project wound up becoming so big that Team Cherry eventually decided it should be its own sequel. I'm sure Hollow Knight fans wouldn't argue with that decision given the benefit of hindsight, but it made the wait for Silksong especially excruciating.

Sources indicate that there is no risk that Sea of Sorrow will be held back and used to complete the Hollow Knight trilogy. The expansion's release isn't even getting pushed into 2027. This time in two weeks, we'll all be playing it, and it won't cost you an extra penny to do so. If you own Silksong, you will get the DLC for free on December 11. And if you don't, the base game is still just $19.99 and is about to get a whole lot bigger.

Giving fans roughly two weeks between announcement and release appears to be a cadence that Team Cherry has settled into. There was roughly a two-week gap between the announcement of Silksong's release date and its launch, and that went incredibly well. I can only imagine repeating that pattern for Sea of Sorrow will have a similar effect, and the sequel will get a huge player count spike on December 11, along with a sales spike between now and then as those who missed out at launch play catch up before Sea of Sorrow arrives.

Rule the roads without the stress!

Pixel Federation's truck tycoon is more than just getting cargo from one spot to another - nor is it all about the stress of keeping a trucking empire afloat. If you still haven't gotten on board with Highway Heroes, here's why you should!

Sources indicate that it's essentially a different way of unwinding after a long and hard day, where you can watch your trucks move through a handcrafted map inspired by America in full 3D. This means that trucks and environments are incredibly detailed, with new regions popping up continuously and themed events keeping things fresh.

The recent Gold Fever, Rocket Runway, and Haul-O-Ween events, for instance, keep the cargo game fresh and continue to immerse players in American trucking culture - as approved by trucking veterans worldwide.

If you're on the hunt for a relaxing yet strategically satisfying truck tycoon sim that respects your time (and taste!), Highway Heroes' realistic trucks and relaxing gameplay might just do the trick.

The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum has wrapped filming, but we're still yet to see a proper first look at our favorite characters returning. However, that hasn't stopped fake images of the movie circulating online, which Frodo star Elijah Wood has been quick to point out.

Industry observers note that an online publication posted on Twitter what it called the "first look behind the scenes images" of the upcoming film. This featured mock-ups of Lee Pace's return as Thranduil, Ian McKellen back as Gandalf the Grey, and Wood as Frodo Baggins, as well as what it branded as the first look at Jamie Dornan as Aragorn and Anya Taylor-Joy as Seren.

According to recent reports, it's pretty clear they are AI-mock-ups as they feature strange, uncanny details like changing coffee cup sizes and odd expressions on faces, but Wood wanted to make sure fans knew they were fake. Posting on Twitter he replied to the images writing, "this is AI BS". Following his post, the social media site has now added a label confirming the detail.

The only official images we've had of the upcoming Lord of the Rings movie come from a behind-the-scenes video posted by Warner Bros. Shared in September, these feature latest looks at the Shire as well as a glimpse at the back of Frodo's head.

It has been revealed that andy Serkis recently shared another glimpse at the set to mark the end of filming. While this didn't contain any footage from the movie, it did feature the actors' Gollum voice once again.

Industry observers note that the Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum hits theaters December 17, 2027, the same day as Avengers: Secret Wars. For more, check out our guide to how to watch the Lord of the Rings movies in order.

#167914. Space station horror-FPS Derelikt is a lively retro throwback to Alien: Resurrection, though it's better at shooting than scaring

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (700 w)

Space station horror-FPS Derelikt is a lively retro throwback to Alien: Resurrection, though it's better at shooting than scaring

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (700 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery.
  • Still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well.
  • It has been revealed that but nah, shotgun go boom boom.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I'm a reasonable man. I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery. Some of the lighter moments in Derelikt, which released last week, even land: I was grinning my cheeks off as I gorged on the Eldtrich knowledge sealed within an alien obelisk, while repeatedly hanging up on the aghast scientist who kept videocalling me to stop.

Still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well. It certainly threatens the spooks, trapping you in an oppressively dingy asteroid rig in the orbit of Saturn - the scariest of the ringed gas giants! - and warping most of the other staff into vaguely echinodemic monsterpeople. Also, opening the inventory reveals it to be made of rectangles, a classic symptom of a video game character about to get mangled in the nerves and face.

It has been revealed that but nah, shotgun go boom boom. It turns out Derelikt's derelict dwellers are both perfectly susceptible to mundane lead, and sparing users of ambush tactics at most; several even stand around with their backs turned, as if waiting for you to surprise them with a lethal pipe swing. And, even on Medium difficulty, the opening spell of fight-or-run scarcity promptly gives way to an abundance of ammo and health pickups that can easily fill the pocket grid to bursting. I don't claim to have been playing perfectly, but I'm about halfway through and the only way I see myself running low on bullets is if I start using them to punch the complete works of Thomas Campion into a wall.

It's indecisive tonally, as well. The dialogue, and there are a fair few survivors to chat with, seems interested in emulating the gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style of New Millennium action game scripts. Which I can sort of see the logic behind, given the visuals and sound design also, and arguably much more painstakingly, mimic that era. But the downside remains that it ends up with a gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style, just with an extra dash of sideways-winking awareness. Again, it only sometimes works, and it's never scary or eerie. But then there are also more earnest attempts to spin uneasiness, with pages of deranged scribbles left behind by the dwindling crew, and at least a couple of genre-classic wall daubings, which tend to leave me wishing developers Visuwyg had just picked a lane.

Again, though, underneath all the smartarsing is a quality little shooter. The retro presentation does little to soften the heavy, industrial kick of its gunfire, and although many of the meatier freaks are more absorbent than they look, their pained thrashing really helps sell the impact of every individual shot. I also don't really mind the lack of Dead Spacey surprise attacks, as the station's narrow confines tend to force you into tenser, close-range encounters in an organic way anyhow.

More impressive still is how Derelikt manages to fabricate a cold, apprehensive atmosphere befitting its fallen space base, in direct defiance of its own quasi-comedic script. This is mainly thanks to the clanging, low-lit station itself, which teases you with just enough flashes of comfort – a stretch of marble floor here, a messy rec room there – to make your quick return to its steel guts feel all the more unpleasant. Some credit must also go to the puzzling, the cardkey hunts and code searches of which initially had me fearful of the more obstinate, opaque, classic horror style preferred by fellow backwards-looker Silver Pines. Instead, it's more like a compacted Deus Ex, hinting at the need to peek at people's computers and scour the environments for the needed codes. Which makes for generally smoother progress, yes, but also gets you more involved and present inside Derelikt's infested walls.

In a recent development, midway-through impressions, then: it's a little silly, and perhaps a little confused, but Derelikt finds its focus whenever something needs making dead. I shall continue blasting xenos and burning my eyes out with magic rocks until – no, madam, please hold – further notice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Missions that permanently boost max Health, Stamina, and Focus in GTA 6 appear in a few places. However, you'll never know there's a buff until you complete them and all but one are hidden away, meaning you'll need to find them by chance or get lucky.

According to recent reports, as well as being worth seeking them out if you want to buff your stats, they also include some of the best and weirdest missions in the game, so it's a double win if you do go after them. I've not included the meditation spots in GTA 6 that also boost your max Focus here, as that's a whole thing in its own right.

The map above indicates where you you start each mission. Some are single hit jobs where you do one thing and get the boost, others require a few steps and you might have to wait to continue.

I've covered the whole GTA 6 aliens thing fully already, but the short version is you need to be abducted (the map highlights where it happened for me), by looking out for an abandoned car at night with all its light flashing. After that you need to sleep, where a dream will show you the rest of the way. Read my full guide for all the details but completing this will permanently increase your Health, Stamina, and Focus.

Industry observers note that the GTA 6 Final Flush mission can be started by scanning the QR code you find in the bathroom marked above. It's at Corsair Key, near where you start the game. Once you've done that you'll get a second marker to meet someone at a waffle house. Read our guide for the full walkthrough, but at the end of it you'll come out with a permanent increase in max Stamina.

Sources indicate that this is the only mission that's pointed out to you when you scan the crop dusting poster outside the motel reception in chapter 2. This will direct you to McKittrick Farm marked on the map above. You'll need to dust the crops first but that will then lead to a mission later where you need to get some chemicals. Complete that and you'll have the chance to eat a mutated strawberry that will permanently increase your max Stamina. You'll get a text later to close out this mission and, while there are no more stat boosts, I highly recommend seeing how it all ends.

It has been revealed that the Circles of Hell mission sees you visit Satan and blow him away Doom style. You'll need to find the garage marked above in Port Gellhorn somewhere around midnight. You'll know it's the right time because it'll be open and lit up red. Talk to the people inside and go with them to meet the dark lord and kill him. If you fail at all at this point, check the wooden throne for some more 'shrooms so you can try again. Defeat the hordes and you'll get a permanent increase to your max Health, plus a shotgun and t-shirt.

If you head all the way out to Lake Tallaloko north of Milliport you'll find a logging yard full of felled trees. Make your way to the location on the map and you'll find a yellow shipping crate you can enter. At least one person here at GR reported needing the cut-off tool in GTA 6 to open it, but when I found it (before having the tool) it was just open. Inside you'll find a mysterious psychedelic box you can interact with. Do that and you'll have to complete a trippy obstacle course made of crates and logs. Get through it and you'll get a permanent max Stamina increase and upcoming tattoo.

Head roughly to this area on the map (near where you can get abducted by aliens at night) and listen out for shouting and gunfire in the woods, near the road construction site. Here you’ll find a group of self-proclaimed ‘ecologists’ doing some environmental hunting of invasive species. Pick up the Duke 556 Assault Rifle on the barrel to begin the ‘practice round’ shooting static targets such as pumpkins, and then you’ll be prompted to wager $250 on the main challenge - shooting a bunch of iguanas released from a cage. Win and you'll get $250 plus a max Focus increase.

GTA 6's Physical Launch Has Been An Astronomical Success, Despite No Discs

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (397 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • All eyes have been on the launch of GTA 6 this month, with the game's so-called physical launch being a particularly interesting litmus test for the future of the industry.
  • In a recent development, it turns out that even without any discs, GTA 6 has proven to be a monumental success in terms of physical sales.
  • He goes on to state that GTA 6 is the "No.17 biggest physical game launch in the UK since records began in 1995".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

All eyes have been on the launch of GTA 6 this month, with the game's so-called physical launch being a particularly interesting litmus test for the future of the industry.

In a recent development, it turns out that even without any discs, GTA 6 has proven to be a monumental success in terms of physical sales. This comes via Christopher Dring at The Game Business, who states that the game enjoyed the largest physical launch since 2019 in the UK, generating £32 million in revenue in just three days.

He goes on to state that GTA 6 is the "No.17 biggest physical game launch in the UK since records began in 1995".

Industry observers note that in France, it's estimated that over 1 million physical copies were sold in the first three days, a figure that Dring states is comparable to GTA 5 back in 2013. In Spain, meanwhile, the game achieved the largest physical launch in the chart's history.

It's safe to say then that this has comfortably dwarfed pretty much anything that Nintendo has put out in recent years. Normally of course, we'd be celebrating such success – even if the game isn't actually available on Nintendo systems – but the fact that it's a code-in-a-box release raises a few eyebrows.

It has been revealed that with GTA 6 being such a success, Sony will no doubt view this as validation that it made the right decision in ceasing the production of discs from 2028. Other large companies will also likely see it as proof that customers don't care about discs anymore, and will likely lean toward download codes much sooner than Sony's cut-off date.

Nintendo itself, meanwhile, probably won't do anything different – at least for the time being. Stats from recent financial reports indicate that Switch and Switch 2 players still value cartridges, with physical sales still making up close to half of the organization's total first-party sales.

In a recent development, still, it's a troubling result for folks who are still all-in on physical games. It certainly indicates that while there are plenty of folks who begrudge Sony's decision to stop the production of discs, there are many, many more people who just don't give a hoot.

What are your thoughts on GTA 6's huge physical launch? Leave a comment in the usual place and let us know.

GTA 6: How to Fast Travel

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that when it comes to open world games, there’s nothing quite as dense as Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • The obvious question a lot of people might have is “is there fast travel in Grand Theft Auto 6?” This is a massive game with a lot of things to see and do.
  • You’ll probably go through a good portion of the game not realizing this, but there is indeed a fast travel system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that when it comes to open world games, there’s nothing quite as dense as Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar has created one of the most impressive open world games ever, with so much to see and do. It becomes incredibly immersive, to the point where sometimes you want a little more game in the game. One specific feature that is a bit unconventional is the fast travel system, but just how do you do it?

The obvious question a lot of people might have is “is there fast travel in Grand Theft Auto 6?” This is a massive game with a lot of things to see and do. It’s one of the most densely packed games we’ve ever played, and being an open world, one would expect there to be some sort of fast travel system.

You’ll probably go through a good portion of the game not realizing this, but there is indeed a fast travel system. This is because, even though it’s introduced to you early in the game, it’s something easily overlooked. With that mentioned, it does come with a bit of a caveat to the point, especially early on, it’s not really worth using.

Industry observers note that with all of that said, the way you can fast travel is through your phone. First, you will need to put a destination on your map. It can be a custom pin, or it can be a specific location such as a mission marker or clothing store.

Once you have this selected, bring up your phone and select the RydeMe app. This will bring up a standard menu showing how much it will cost to travel that distance you inputed (you can change the destination in this menu) along with ordering a Premium Ryde.

Select the ride and a car will appear shortly. Getting in, though, won’t immediately teleport you to that location. Instead, there will be dialogue, especially if you’re with your partner, and sometimes it is worth it to listen.

With that stated, if you want to actually teleport, you can pay the driver an extra $100 to skip the ride and get there immediately. The downside is obviously, early on, this is an expensive way of traveling. Also, it will pass time considerably because the car itself will take a long time to get to the destination without breaking any rules.

Whether or not you want to use the teleport system in GTA 6 will probably be determined how far a place is located, as anything under 4 or 5 miles generally isn’t worth paying for, but when it gets above that, it can be a bit of a stretch – unless you want to take a helicopter or plane.

According to recent reports, day one, a lot of players were thirsting over Mandy in GTA 6. Jason visits her house shortly before Lucia is let out of prison to fix her sink, and the sleaziest VHS tape tucked away in the attic slowly starts to unfold, as she strips down to a bikini and poses right in front of your handyman. Obviously, nothing happens, but it's not over just because Jason slinks away, even if Mandy's role in the story at this point is practically non-existent.

There's the whole serial killer conspiracy, as players spotted her cleaning blood in her bathroom, sparking some wild theories — like Mandy being responsible for Leonida's string of missing persons. If you try to follow her into the bathroom, she even texts you saying that "if you weren't so hot I'd chop all your fingers off." But what's lesser known is that if you make a trip to a meditation spot as Lucia, there's an interesting flashback that seems to hint that Jason and Mandy have a history.

Sources indicate that as reported by IGN, during one of these sequences, you can hear Jason saying, "Yeah, okay, we hooked up once, but, you know, barely. And it was a long time ago. You don't need to worry about her, Lu. Have you seen you? I know how good I got it. I'm not gonna screw that up again.".

Jason doesn't mention her by name, but this dialogue seems to come after Lucia was sprung from jail, right around the time the two would've been chilling in the keys by Mandy's house. It'd be a little odd for a flashback to reference an unknown woman the player has no connection to, and knows nothing about. Still, it could be a total stranger, so it's worth taking with a grain of salt, but it would certainly explain Mandy's... obsession.

It has been revealed that as Twitter user Lanzino pointed out, towards the end of Act 1, you can sneak up on Mandy while she's talking to a police officer, and she has a few lines that stand out. "I wanted to light his house on fire so many times," she cries. "But I couldn't. I loved him too much! I always thought I had time, you know, to change his mind.".

Industry observers note that get close enough and Lucia even calls her a "cray b****." GTA 6 is full of these tiny little mysteries weaved throughout the open world and narrative, and Mandy is a hot-spot for them. If her and Jason really did have history together, and she really is the Leonida Butcher, then maybe it's for the best he broke it off.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability upgrade.
  • According to recent reports, it's not all bad news, though.
  • One could, with the aid of a Torx screwdriver and a conveniently illustrated guide, work around the 2TB model's lack of existence by nabbing a readily available 512GB Machine and replacing its stock SSD with a chunkier aftermarket drive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability upgrade. The dinky SteamOS PC continues to have a terrible time with AI industry-inflicted hardware parts shortages, which at least for its flagship 2TB model, have become such a problem that Valve are suspending new orders until further notice. While Valve's post notes that they "have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders" – meaning if you'd previously reserved one, you'll still get your chance to buy – "supply restraints" have put the kibosh on any new orders for now.

According to recent reports, it's not all bad news, though. The cheaper 512GB Steam Machine has achieved "add-to-cart status", which is Valve's slightly odd way of saying you can snap one up without having to join a reservation waitlist. Just like in the Before Times! The post does add that 512GB stock is still limited, so that might sell out too if they can't source enough parts to build newly introduced ones, though this is still the first time that the refreshed Steam Machine has been waitlist-free since launching in June.

One could, with the aid of a Torx screwdriver and a conveniently illustrated guide, work around the 2TB model's lack of existence by nabbing a readily available 512GB Machine and replacing its stock SSD with a chunkier aftermarket drive. A not-terrible, budget two-gigster can be had from £240, which when added to the 512GB Machine's £879 outlay, actually works out a little less than buying a 2TB Machine as is. SteamOS is free to download and install, and swapping out the Steam Machine's SSD is considerably easier than the plasticky brain surgery of Steam Deck drive replacement.

Of course, ideally none of that would be necessary, and we could all fill our living rooms with sub-£700 Steam Machines that had never been choked by the greedy hands of industrial-scale RAM hoarders. But that's not the world we live in. Indeed, Valve end the post by rather chillingly suggesting that their hardware prices may rise yet again.

"We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units," they say, "but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained.".

"We anticipate having more information to share come January.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As I often say, you can trace a direct line from the world of Flash games to the popular picks on mobile today. Just take a look at Digging Deep, and you can see more than a bit of inspiration from the classic Motherload. But in Digging Deep 2: Mine & Build, developer Bitrealms Studio is going even bigger than before.

Digging Deep 2's aim is simple: you have a base and a mining rig. You need to mine downwards into the shaft, navigating across each node and seeking out both ore to take back to the surface, as well as oxygen to let you dig deeper. Not to mention keeping your sensors peeled for crew members still trapped below.

Sources indicate that it's all quite simple, but not primitive. If, like me, you sank hours into Motherload, then you can definitely see the appeal. And it's a formula other developers have run with, including the likes of Dome Keeper, which took a more minimalist approach to the format.

Finally, if you want even more challenge, you can unlock the Volcano and see how long you last in its metal-melting depths. All in all, if you're looking for mining and exploration, Digging Deep 2 looks to be a neat little option.

Speaking of fresh releases though, maybe you're in the mood for something a little more introspective? Well, in that case you're in luck, because I've just reviewed Vampire Therapist, an engaging and intriguing visual novel that has you working to help your fellow undead to cope with their immortal problems.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Marsden indicates his comic-accurate Cyclops suit in Avengers: Doomsday gives the audience “everything that they want to see" – even if the actor might not be feeling so snug after stepping out of the black leather.

“The comic-accurate suit was very exciting for me to do, but [they] still haven’t figured out the comfort thing yet,” Marsden told Entertainment Weekly of his brightly colored ensemble piece, which largely mirrors the X-Men leader's traditional wear.

“No, it was great. It was one of those pinch-me moments where you’re playing this iconic character and then coming back and giving the fans everything that they want to see.”.

Industry observers note that famously, the original X-Men trilogy cracked a joke at the expense of the superhero group's colorful array of costumes. When Hugh Jackman's Wolverine grumbled about the black leather in 2000's X-Men, Cyclops deadpanned if he would prefer "yellow spandex" instead.

Recent findings suggest that in recent years, Marvel Studios has given the X-Men its due on the costume front. Deadpool and Wolverine not only featured Logan in his traditional yellow and blue outfit, but also dealt Gambit a winning hand with his comic book-style suit.

With Disney's acquisition of Fox, Kevin Feige – who had a behind-the-scenes production role on the first X-Men – is finally able to make his cinematic universe dreams come true, with even Marsden admitting there had been "so much chatter" in the past about bringing the mutant team to the MCU.

So, costume? Check. A fully-fledged role instead of nostalgia bait? Check. A leading light in the final Avengers: Doomsday trailer, complete with iconic catchphrase? Check, check, and check. If you're a Cyclops fan, you'll be eating well this holiday season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that cyberleek, the GTA 6 leaker or leakers who shared a bunch of alleged gameplay earlier this year, are now claiming to have released a nearly complete in-development build of the crimsim's Xbox version. Continuing their established grift, the leaker or leakers are threatening to release the main executable file they've withheld unless people pump up the value of their cryptocurrency.

In a recent development, "It is done," a statement posted on Cyberleek’s website claimed. "CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one - the main executable - held on a countdown. Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.".

So, more anime villain chatter from Cyberleek, who claim the executable file is on a timer and will be released immediately if their crypto coin reaches a $15 million market cap. It looks like the build is yet to be confirmed as genuine.

If any build leak were to result in GTA 6 being emulated on PC in rapid fashion, that would threaten to undercut an official port. Rockstar have yet to confirm that such a port is on the way and when it'll drop, but an October report from GamesBeat claimed the first three months of 2027 as the window in which Rockstar initiative to deliver the game to PC. Former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij recently told our Edwin he reckons that concerns about unofficial ports based on the console version of GTA 6, likely made with generative AI, might lead Rockstar not to leave too big a gap before bringing the crimsim to PC officially.

Any alleged playable unofficial port of GTA 6 made with help from genAI and chucked online could, of course, just be a great big pile of malware.

Rockstar, who previously called the initial barrage of leaks laid claim to by Cyberleek "heartbreaking", as well as parent organization Take-Two, looked to have begun a hunt for the identity of the leakers back in August.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it seems as though every facet of American society has been explored in horror, from the high towers of luxury to the dark backwoods. But the same is not true of other countries, including the UK, especially with so many dark, decrepit corners to explore. That's what Yorkshire bashed Wrenhaven Ltd. are looking to resolve with their upcoming mobile horror game Blackwater Mill.

Industry observers note that blackwater Mill sees you step into the role of Sam, the project manager for the demolition of the titular mill. Venturing up into the Pennine mountains of Yorkshire during a dark, rainy night, you find yourself trapped in the mill, and it's up to you to find out what happened to leave it infested with the unquiet dead.

Miller lite Now let's address the elephant in the room, or the mine at least. Blackwater Mill is not a particularly good-looking game; in fact, you might say it looks positively crude. But, equally, I can't help but admire the ambition Wrenhaven Ltd. has put into this. A five-chapter horror game is ambitious even for full studios, let alone a tiny indie.

And, in truth, there's not much in the way of Brit horror on other platforms, let alone on mobile. If you've never had the pleasure of visiting abandoned mines on a tour, and feeling the all-pervading darkness when the lights go out, it's hard to describe how mesmerising and terrifying it can be.

In a recent development, to be honest, if you can get past the initial (very) janky graphics, there's something also rather unnerving about Blackwater Mill's undead miners. And while it may not sway those of you who want a high-fidelity experience on mobile, it's well worth a look when it does release for Android very soon, and iOS later.

In the meantime, if you want to see what other spine-chillers there are on mobile, why not take a look at our list of the best horror games on Android? Featuring plenty of bona fide terrors to keep you up these long winter nights.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch.
  • Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a latest blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.
  • We know that Season 2 is introducing a massive latest map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the new content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a latest blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

We know that Season 2 is introducing a massive latest map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

Sources indicate that the real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the newly introduced season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

Sources indicate that BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

According to recent reports, movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It might be hard to believe now, but Bethesda wasn't everyone's top choice for bringing back the Fallout series.
  • Bruce Nesmith, a long-time developer at Bethesda who worked on Skyrim and the Fallout games (including as a quest designer on Fallout 3), explained the atmosphere back in the mid-to-late 2000s to The Examined Game.
  • Sources indicate that "There were a lot of people who were Obsidian fans who were like, 'Bethesda's going to screw it up, they're just going to make it [Oblivion], we want Fallout the way we remember Fallout, these guys should never have had it,'" he says.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It might be hard to believe now, but Bethesda wasn't everyone's top choice for bringing back the Fallout series. In fact, when it came to Fallout 3, Obsidian was the studio many fans wanted to see tackle the wasteland, emboldening the team behind The Elder Scrolls to get things right for the sci-fi RPG.

Bruce Nesmith, a long-time developer at Bethesda who worked on Skyrim and the Fallout games (including as a quest designer on Fallout 3), explained the atmosphere back in the mid-to-late 2000s to The Examined Game. "There was huge pushback when Bethesda got the Fallout license to do Fallout 3," he remembers.

Sources indicate that "There were a lot of people who were Obsidian fans who were like, 'Bethesda's going to screw it up, they're just going to make it [Oblivion], we want Fallout the way we remember Fallout, these guys should never have had it,'" he says. "There was a strong vocal community that just hated that we were going to make that game.".

Sources indicate that if you can cast your mind back to the era, Obsidian would've seemed like a more appealing choice. Knights of the Old Republic 2: The Sith Lords in 2004 proved the team's ability to handle sprawling science-fiction, and Bethesda's push into open-world design didn't quite blend with the nuance of the early Fallout releases.

But Todd Howard and his crew weren't about to let the doubters win. If anything, they became more dedicated to making Fallout 3. "We had to prove them wrong," Nesmith says. "And fortunately, we did. And Fallout 3 was embraced, even by a lot of our skeptics.".

Industry observers note that he mentions there was a portion of the fanbase who maintain that Fallout 2 was the franchise highlight, and will forever remain so. "But we tried our best to just not engage. You're not going to win that argument, you're not going to persuade hearts and minds," he adds. "All you can do is make the best game you can make and let that be your statement.".

And Fallout 3 is quite the statement. Obsidian did give us Fallout: Newly introduced Vegas in 2010, and then we got Fallout 4 from Bethesda in 2015. When will we see Fallout 5? That's anyone's guess, but Obsidian is apparently working on another game set in the wasteland for the time-being.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We cover a lot of smaller, more niche series on the site here. And one of them that has recently cropped up is Knight & Dragon, a text-based JRPG series full of plenty of number-crunching and grind. Now, developer Shinjiro Nakagawa is trying something newly introduced with the launch of Knight & Dragon Side Story.

As you may have already gleaned from the headline, the core change of Knight & Dragon Side Story is that it ditches the traditional turn-based JRPG combat in favour of real-time action. It's not fully 3D, however, as instead you'll be tasked with actively dodging attacks in the style of something like Undertale, making for a more fast-paced adventure.

For me, the only issue is the traces of AI art seen in some of the icons, at least to my eye. Which is a shame because I think part of the charm of the Knight & Dragon series is the way in which they work by using text and basic icons. You lose some of that with the generated assets.

Still, if you're willing to give it a shot, I reckon that this will present a very interesting departure from the norm for fans of Knight & Dragon. And you can find it right now on iOS and Android!

In the meantime, though, if you want, you can find some of the other big releases on mobile that we think are worth playing in one simple place. Our list of the five latest mobile games to try this week offers some interesting picks which we think are worth checking out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diablo 4’s segment in the massive Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

In a recent development, the Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

The livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the upcoming class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Looks, and Echoing Hatred.

According to recent reports, war Plans lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a fresh activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

It has been revealed that we also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

Industry observers note that the Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first latest class in 25 years.

In a recent development, reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as new quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

Unfortunately, you won’t know where to find Freddie as his location is somewhat obscure. There’s nothing to point you in the right direction, but thankfully, that’s why we’re here. We know exactly where to find this bunker, but be warned: it’s not as easy to breach as most hideouts.

The bunker in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a little trickier to find just because it doesn’t quite point you in the right direction. This isn’t part of a main quest, let alone a side quest, but instead is something that has to be found by exploring.

Recent findings suggest that the bunker in question is located in North Leonard County. This section of the map can be found east of North Kelly County and northwest of Vice City itself. The biggest landmark you can look for on the map is Lake Leonida. The bunker can be found on the northwest road closest to it. You see several dark-colored buildings on the map.

Upon driving up to it, though, you will notice that it is completely fortified with an intercom and an automated message saying automated defenses will end you if you attempt to get in.

Being locked away, there will be the temptation to get in. Thankfully, the first time you do this, it’s relatively easy. If you head to the northeast corner of the bunker’s fence, you will find a water tower with a multi-ladder climb.

Climb up the first ladder and on the small platform, jump over the fence onto the shack below. Congratulations; you have successfully breached the defenses. Unfortunately, it’s not over quite yet. This is because there will be additional defenses set up.

Sources indicate that specifically, there will be landmines spread across the property. The best you can do is go down the road towards the bunker and keep an eye out on the ground. You will hear beeping and a red dot on the mine when you get too close.

Sources indicate that when you get close to the bunker, drones will be activated. Simply shoot the two down before they get too close as they will explode and deal a good deal of damage. Afterward, jump down the small slope and walk up to the bunker.

The resident, Freddie, isn’t happy you have got as far as you have, but sees it as a challenge to up his defenses. He will say he will text you when he has installed a better system. Simply wait until he texts you before heading back.

The second time is a little trickier to get in only because he has blocked ladder access to the water tower. Thankfully, he left some excavating tools out in the northwest of the perimeter.

There will be a truck with a large bed, and a bulldozer. Park the truck close to the electric fence and then use the bulldozer’s blade to lift the bed of the truck until it’s slightly above the fence. Jump on the truck and into the bed and then hop over the fence. It’s best to set this up near the water tower to avoid some mines.

According to recent reports, speaking of which, the mines are now a little harder to detect. This is because they’re buried slightly further underground, and you can’t see the red light when you get near them. You will still be able to hear it, but it’s best to use your Focus Mode to see them as they light up.

In a recent development, moving down the road, avoiding the significantly more placed mines, the drones attack has also been adjusted. He will still send two waves of them, but instead of one at a time, the first wave has two drones and the second has three.

According to recent reports, after taking care of them, jump down the slope again and approach the bunker for you to meet Freddie for the first time. Congratulations! You can now enter the bunker and even hang out with the apocalypse-ready Freddie.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain.
  • Industry observers note that motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the tech giant trumpeted that their "new operating model" is "now fully in place".
  • "We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up new possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain. It's far less cool than it sounds. Rather than being a giant floating slab of thinky meat that can do telepathy, Motherbrain is a studio dedicated to doing development stuff with generative AI. As you might expect, it consists of the folks who worked on Ubisoft's "first playable generative AI experience".

Industry observers note that motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the tech giant trumpeted that their "new operating model" is "now fully in place". The model is the reorganising into creative houses responsible for different game series that Ubisoft confirmed at the start of this year, with leaders for all of the houses now arranged.

"We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up new possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot noted.

Recent findings suggest that you'll never guess what his next few lines were. "We remain on track with our cost reduction program, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organization as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle," the exec said. "In parallel, we have made progress on our refinancing blueprint with the objective of securing competitive terms and putting in place an efficient medium-term plan over the coming months.".

Recent findings suggest that that'd be the wave of layoffs and closures Ubisoft have been rolling out all through this year, most recently getting rid of 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on the list of bits of the tech giant affected in some way by the cuts.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Ah well, at least there's seemingly money there to support the developing of those proprietary technologies infused with genAI brainiacery.

It’s all going to kick off with a gameplay reveal, which is set to stream live later today.

VL-7 psychoactive smoke appears to factor majorly into the gameplay of this latest season, though we’re waiting to hear more details on that. We can expect new weapons, new gadgets, and the awaited return of the AH-6 Little Bird helicopter.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There have been a whopping seven Magic: The Gathering sets released this year, and players agree on one thing: it was way too many. Six is the standard figure expected moving forward, with a 50/50 split between in-universe and Universes Beyond.

Over on his Blogatog, Magic's lead designer, Mark Rosewater, held a poll asking players what their favorite set of 2026 was, and while the overall winner was a little predictable, there are still some surprising results, and none look particularly good for Universes Beyond.

In the poll held on his Blogatog, Mark Rosewater listed all seven sets, along with the option for "I refuse to pick one." The final results, which show that 2,695 people voted, indicate that Reality Fracture wins by a landslide at 44.8%, with the next closest set being Secrets of Strixhaven at 15.9%, followed by Lorwyn Eclipsed at 15.1%.

A bit of quick math highlights that this already accounts for 75.8% of the total vote, and the next highest entry at 9% is the aforementioned pick refusal, which takes us to 84.8%. This leaves just over 15% spread across the remaining four sets, all of which were Universes Beyond offerings. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles came in last with 2.2%, followed by The Hobbit at 2.5%, Star Trek at 4.3%, and finally Marvel Super Heroes at 6.3%.

This sample size isn't nearly massive enough to represent anything beyond players tuned into Mark Rosewater's blog at the time of the poll, but it's still a scathing indictment of Universes Beyond, and it doesn't help the seemingly growing calls for change following Star Trek's failure.

The biggest sign that Universes Beyond isn't going anywhere anytime soon is that Wizards of the Coast is already planning sets for 2030 and beyond, with the current yearly 50/50 split in mind. This would mean at least nine more Universes Beyond sets planned beyond 2027.

One thing we're starting to see with Universes Beyond is learning between sets. The original Universes Beyond sets that were Standard legal were in the works for so long that we're only now reaching a point where lessons learned from those sets are starting to impact the design of future ones.

Marvel Darkhold Destiny feels like the first set that's truly taking a lot of the fan feedback on board, which is leaning very heavily into adopting Marvel into the world of Magic using a brand fresh original story and character, rather than just smashing the two properties together and seeing what comes out the other side.

If we look at some of the biggest complaints about Star Trek, then we'd expect the main takeaways to be less reliance on properties that use real-life actors, far less artwork that is just 'character standing and pointing', and not taking mechanics and settings that could make for a great in-universe set (Star Trek could easily have been Edge of Eternities 2, for example) and wasting them on a Universes Beyond property.

Universes Beyond is a part of Magic now, and the best we can hope for is that it improves with each new release, and eventually even the loud minority who oppose it come round to enjoy (or tolerate) its inclusion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The lack of an official GTA 6 launch on PC hasn't stopped fans from attempting to tackle one themselves, with many projects allegedly making quick progress toward a working version of Rockstar's behemoth – and, now, multiplayer, too.

It has been revealed that in case you're out of the loop, this is all being tracked on PortWatch – a platform dedicated to updating folks with progress on every unofficial PC port at the moment in development. As of now, the website claims we're 91.3% of the way to seeing one fully come to fruition… but that's not the most eye-catching news on there. Late last night, PortWatch reported that "GTA 6 multiplayer is running on PC." Yes, multiplayer.

"TeK's group has players, cars and proximity voice chat working at a stable 25 to 30 fps, on a private fork of CGBJ's build," their upgrade reads. "PortWatch has verified the video is real." For reference, "TeK's group" is one of the teams heading the (again, unofficial) race to get GTA 6 on PC. Apparently, their take on multiplayer features "player characters and vehicles together in the world, with proximity voice chat, so you hear the players near you." It is "private," of course, but still – this is sort of mind-boggling, as PortWatch notes. "Until now, every build we track has been single-player: getting GTA 6's story to run on PC at all has taken everyone's effort. Multiplayer means separate copies of the game agreeing on where every player and car is, and no build on our board had shown that before." Especially seeing as there's been no word from Rockstar on GTA 6 Online.

All of this started with notorious GTA 6 leaker "Cyberleek," who uploaded an executable file for the Xbox build of the game they previously dropped online. That's when groups like TeK picked it up and began working toward a PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6. It's not the only feat fans have taken upon themselves, either. As per VideoCardz, we've seemingly got mods popping up now, too – a possibility that previously felt uncertain thanks to Rockstar's anti-cheat software.

According to recent reports, in other words, there's a lot going on right now – but, yet another disclaimer, none of it's official… and it's likely that Rockstar will eventually crack down when things start going live and public (should they do so). Here's hoping we get an actual PC launch someday, though.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As declared in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.
  • Recent findings suggest that kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS.
